Tailored interventions, such as telephone counseling, may be effective in promoting change among nonadherent women who are at risk of missing mammography screening. These interventions seem to be more powerful than tailored print communications for getting nonadherent women on schedule for the recommended mammography screenings. However, it is essential to answer additional questions about why these tailored interventions might not have been more effective and what factors contribute to adherence in this population.

While telephone counseling has shown promising results in promoting change among nonadherent women, further research is needed to understand its mechanisms of action and potential limitations. Additionally, the relative risk of CV outcomes associated with severe hypoglycaemia compared to tailored print communications highlights the importance of considering individual health needs when developing interventions.

It is also essential to acknowledge that adherence to mammography screening can be influenced by various factors beyond individual-level interventions, including healthcare provider recommendations (in this case, simple prompts geared towards identifying high-risk patients). Future studies should investigate the utility of these prompts and explore how they compare to other methods for improving adherence to follow-up recommendations.
